title: No public security.txt endpoint observed on the www host

evidence.observation: GET https://www.cynbit.in/.well-known/security.txt and GET https://www.cynbit.in/security.txt each returned 404.

impact: A researcher may have difficulty locating a preferred coordinated vulnerability disclosure channel. This is a security-hygiene issue and does not demonstrate an exploitable vulnerability or compromise.
remediation: Publish and maintain an RFC 9116 security.txt at /.well-known/security.txt on each intended public production host, with a monitored contact and valid Expires value; optionally redirect /security.txt to the well-known resource.
references: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Information Gathering and Configuration and Deployment Management Testing

title: Common browser defense headers absent from sampled homepage response

evidence.observation: The single captured GET response for https://www.cynbit.in/ did not include Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Strict-Transport-Security was present. Finding is limited to this response.

impact: Missing headers reduce defense-in-depth against classes such as content injection, framing, MIME sniffing, and unintended referrer disclosure if a separate weakness exists. No XSS, clickjacking, or exploitability was demonstrated; headers may differ on other routes or at other layers.
remediation: Review all public HTML/API response paths and configure a tested Content-Security-Policy (begin in report-only mode), frame-ancestors and suitable legacy framing policy, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a privacy-appropriate Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy at the actual frontend/edge serving layer. Preserve HSTS; add includeSubDomains only after confirming subdomain readiness.
references: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Configuration and Deployment Management Testing
